item.title: Reaction
item.description: Spending AP, or in the case of AER Monster Rules Dominance Points to act outside one's Turn, usually during another creature's action and on being provided a Trigger of sorts.

item.title: AER Monster Rules
item.description: The enemies should deal enough damage to be considered threats, and take enough damage to be satisfying to dispatch. The statblocks should be lightweight, clear, and easily skimmable for info.While players get AP for their turns, it would be too troublesome to track a 1-12 value for every enemy on the battle map. As such, for the convenience of the DM, the Action Clusters were developed, monsters get limited Action Clusters. Example Action Cluster Actions would be; 1 AC cost: Move 3 Spaces and make a single weapon attack, if possible. 2 AC cost: Make a ground slam AoE attack. 4 AC cost: Open a portal to the underworld, allowing imps to flood from therein.Dominance is an original system which helps outnumbered enemies shine a bit brighter than usual. The party’s AP Regen is added together, and is divided by the sum of Enemy AC enemies gain 1 Dominance Point at the start of their turn. These allow for a couple of general Dominance Actions, as well as monster-specific ones, giving them a bit of a “last stand” once the players get the upper hand. Sum of Playerside AP Regen / Sum of Enemy Action Clusters = Dominance Points at Round Start Types: meant to give an idea to the DM skimming through the monster manual about how “important” or “influential” an enemy may be. ♕ Centrepiece. 7 AC. 5 DP. ♖ Elite. 5 AC. 3 DP. ♙ Minion. 3 AC. 1 DP.Meant to give insight into how the monster behaves in combat. Most enemies have a combination of two Roles, order does not matter, but some may have the same role twice, highlighting their focus. ♥️ - Brawler. Frontline that's tough to break through. May have area attacks. ♣️ - Commander. Buffs allies, Debuffs enemies. May summon reinforcements. ♦️ - Duellist. Single target focus, high damage, glass cannon, or all three. ♠️ - Skirmisher. Either fully ranged, with ranged capability, or simply a very mobile enemy.Hit Points, Physical and Magical Armours – the general survivability of the monster. Each of these values contributes to the overall durability.

item.title: Spam Penalty
item.description: The second activation of the same Skill Instance in a single turn costs +2 AP per activation. Does not apply to weapon Attacks.

item.title: Round
item.description: The amount of time it takes every creature in Combat to take their Turn. It is usually assumed 6 AP (or 3 AC) worth of Actions takes around 3 seconds, but this conversion is not often useful.

item.title: Turn
item.description: Part of a Round. AER Monster Rules take theirs in a set order, while Players may intervene between those, either one at a time, or all together. Regardless, unless specified otherwise, each creature can only take One Turn per Round.

item.title: Immunity
item.description: Reduces incoming DMG of a given type to 0. Cannot be influenced further.

item.title: Resistance
item.description: Reduces incoming DMG of a given type by 1, to no set minimum. With enough Resistance you may regenerate Vitals, or HP from certain attacks or Skills.

item.title: Hit Points
item.description: This is what AER Monster Rules use when referring to the enemy's Vitals. Reduces confusion between parts relating to Player and Foe, but they are more or less equivalent.

item.title: Heroic Bleedout
item.description:
State activated when Vitals drop below 0. In this state you lose 2 AP Regen for every 1 Vitals below 0. Should your Stored AP reach 0 (either by being taken away through negative Regen, or by one last action), your character Dies.
Alternative: Damsely Faint - when reduced below 0 Vitals you may instead choose to Faint, thus be removed from the Combat and hope your companions can finish the fight without you. Less risk of losing your character, but less agency in what happens next. Great for a bathroom break.

item.title: Cover
item.description: Gives -Dice on ranged attacks regardless of distance. Usually provided by terrain and/or map objects, as well as other creatures.

item.title: Dreadlord
item.description:
Vaguely resemblant of their old selves, these pale creatures have made the ultimate sacrifice for power and eternal life... Vampire - Bloodless: When reduced to 0 Vitals you are killed instantly (no Heroic Bleedout state).
Vampire - Unnatural Physiology: When damaged by Aether, your unnatural physiology is thrown into chaos; take the damage normally, but on the next turn, do not gain your Base Vitals Regen, gaining that value as AP and playing by the standard rules for a round instead.
Vampire - Sacrificial Power: Use Vitals in place of AP.
Any effects that interact with AP, instead interact with Vitals for you.
Eternal Thirst - Sustain: You deal extra Entropy DMG as your Vitals decrease. Gain +1 Entropy DMG per 4 Vitals below your Max.
This extra DMG heals you by 1 when damaging another creature's Hit Points.

item.title: Entropy
item.description:
Entropy: Deals Physical Damage, and does 1 additional damage to exposed Health (Hit Points/Vitals).
It also adds negative effects to Surfaces of Fire and Ice.

item.title: Saurians
item.description:
Ancient lizard/dinosaur people, perhaps older than the Starborn. They lived in a subterranean habitable zone until the Starborn War forced them to the surface, earning the world their grudge... Scaly Skin: Start with 2 INNATE points of Physical and Magical Armour.
Primeval Nature: Can restore full Vitals during Unsafe rests.
Resourceful: When setting up a Sanctuary Rest, a Saurian can automatically check off one of the Requirements.
Old Ways Affinity: -1 SP cost for learning (not upgrading) ProtoMagic Skills.

item.title: Starborn
item.description:
The first race, made by the gods ages ago, with Aether running through their delicate frames. While humanoid from a distance, an up-close look reveals their skin to be made of carved stone, metal, or even ceramics. Their faces are smooth and featureless from the mouth up. They waged the First War and believe themselves superior to other races, especially the short-lived mortal ones. They are now mythic figures pursuing ancient agendas.... Eternal: Start with 3x the alloted starting SP.
Psychic: You perceive the world through a blindsense, being able to sense things through Cover and in all directions, but only up to 30 Hexes.
You may Concentrate (2 Action Points) to narrow Your vision into a 60 Hex line.
Divine Heritage: You are immune to Aether Sickness.

item.title: Ice
item.description: Ice: Deals Physical damage and applies a stack of Brittle. The next Skill or Attack made against a Brittle enemy gets +Dice.

item.title: Fire
item.description: Fire: Can ignite unarmoured targets on a successful roll, dealing 1 additional damage at the start of their next turn. This can continue each turn on a successful roll. Starting a Turn inside a Fire Surface deals 1 Fire DMG.

item.title: Aether
item.description:
Aether: Deals double damage to Undead and Daemons, but heals any other target. Healing through Aether Skills is subject to Aether Sickness.
It also adds beneficial effects to Surfaces of Fire and Ice.

item.title: DMG
item.description:
When a Skill's effect deals magical damage, select one of the following types for it. Aether
Entropy
Fire
Ice
Psychic
Thunder "X" means the surface is cleansed, while "-" means nothing happens to it.

item.title: Daemons
item.description: Celestials whose halo-like head adornments have broken, now resembling tar-black horns. They have no skin, only visible muscle and bone, and can take any form as long as these two constants are maintained... Malleable: Start with ANY 2 New Magic (Flesh Shaping, Hemocrafts), General, Weapon, or Dice Manipulation Skills (1st level only, mix n' match). Silver-tongued: Gain 2x +Dice on interactions with Neutral Creatures, and -Dice on interactions with Friendly Creatures.

item.title: Thunder
item.description: Thunder: On a roll, 1 damage arcs to one additional target within 2 hexes.

item.title: Psychic
item.description: Psychic: Applies -Dice to the target's next action corresponding to any damage amount greater than 1 (e.g., 2 damage becomes 1 damage and 1x -Dice). A single damage point will not apply -Dice, instead dealing damage as normal.

item.title: -Dice
item.description: Modify Resolution. Stackable. For every stack roll an extra die, then pick the lowest value rolled among the results.

item.title: +Dice
item.description: Modify Resolution. Stackable. For every stack roll an extra die, then pick the highest value rolled among the results.

item.title: Creature of the Night
item.description:
Vaguely resemblant of their old selves, these pale creatures have made the ultimate sacrifice for power and eternal life... Vampire - Bloodless: When reduced to 0 Vitals you are killed instantly (no Heroic Bleedout state).
Vampire - Unnatural Physiology: When damaged by Aether, your unnatural physiology is thrown into chaos; take the damage normally, but on the next turn, do not gain your Base Vitals Regen, gaining that value as AP and playing by the standard rules for a round instead.
Vampire - Sacrificial Power: Use Vitals in place of AP.
Any effects that interact with AP, instead interact with Vitals for you.
Eternal Thirst - Devour: Once per combat you may target an adjacent creature, if it has no Physical or Magical Armour points, deal 1 Entropy DMG to it and regain 8 Vitals. This action has no cost but instantly ends your Turn.

item.title: Yig
item.description: Furry, curled-up, hunched-over rat-like creatures with immense intelligence in their beady eyes and mineral formations on their skin. They stay underground, consuming minerals, crystals, and even rock for sustenance. They live in clan-based communities but often venture to the surface for trading or a break from their routines... Hardy: Due to mineral and/or rock consumption, start with either 4 INNATE points of Physical and 2 of Magical Armour, or 2 INNATE points of Physical and 4 of Magical Armour. When starting out, roll 1d12 to establish the amount of protrusions that result from your diet, and will be placed randomly on your inventory grid (1d12 x 1d6 for coordinates). Special Diet: Eats Ores and Minerals for sustenance. Their stomachs can handle regular food but they dislike the overall blandness of it. This includes certain items and goods, which they treat the same way as ultra-processed foods.

item.title: yig (3)
Neo
item.description:
Innovators and industrialists, who exploit Jaddivar and its abundance of resources paired with lack of central leadership - viewed as antagonists by the majority of other races... Human - Ambidextrous: Pick an extra Specialty when starting out. Starchart: Jaddivar-updated Northstar, but with emphasis on communication, navigation, and social status.
Certain information may be redacted, and going against the Neo ideals may even get your instance disconnected.

item.title: Meso
item.description:
Opportunists who surgically removed their implants, and inserted themselves into the existing civilisations, quickly getting familiar and accustomed with the locals and their ways of life... Human - Ambidextrous: Pick an extra Specialty when starting out
Locals: Gain +Dice on interactions with non-hostile creatures.

item.title: neohuman (4)
neohuman (2)
Axi
item.description: Part of the crash landing's population that decided not to interfere with the local order of things, they practice a Solarpunk and isolationist lifestyle, aided by the Northstar AI... Human - Ambidextrous: Pick an extra Specialty when starting out Northstar: An embedded AI-Brain chip allowing incredible information collection, recall, and thinking capabilities, as well as a user-tailored Heads-up-Display. Northstar runs on Earth-gathered data, making it inaccurate and potentially misleading when used on Jaddivar.

item.title: Ar'Darun
item.description: Shorter than humans with enlarged heads, two extra limbs, and sometimes unusual skin pigmentation, giving them an otherworldly appearance. Their origins are speculated to be the result of cross-mutation Neohuman experimental breeding programs... Extra Pair: Reduce Backpack and Equipment handling costs by 1 AP. Includes accessing items, drawing/sheathing weapons, reloading, switching ammo types.

item.title: Pitmaw
item.description:
Majestic, cow-sized canines with four paws and two arms... This one has a permanently open and panting mouth, and broad shoulders... Houndvari - Mount: You can be ridden by creatures smaller than yourself. Houndvari - Gallop: You may spend 2 AP to move 2x+1 Hexes in a straight line. Houndvari - Mule: You can Stack Backpacks of the same type.
I ain't Hear no Bell: The first time You would be reduced to or below 0 Vitals, drop down to 1 instead.

item.title: pit dog
Greyhund
item.description:
Majestic, cow-sized canines with four paws and two arms... This one has an exceptionally large, and wrinkly, head, and stands tall on its paws... Houndvari - Mount: You can be ridden by creatures smaller than yourself. Houndvari - Gallop: You may spend 2 AP to move 2x+1 Hexes in a straight line. Houndvari - Mule: You can Stack Backpacks of the same type.
Old Dog, New Tricks: You may Respec Your SP during a Sanctuary Rest.

item.title: Goodlad
item.description:
Majestic, cow-sized canines with four paws and two arms... This one has very short hair and a sleek, dangerous look... Houndvari - Mount: You can be ridden by creatures smaller than Yourself. Houndvari - Gallop: You may spend 2 AP to move 2x+1 Hexes in a straight line. Houndvari - Mule: You can Stack Backpacks of the same type.
Commanding Presence: Attackers within 1 Hex of You gain -Dice on Attacks against You and Your Allies.

item.title: Dusky
item.description:
Majestic, cow-sized canines with four paws and two arms... This one has rugged and matted fur, and a long snout full of teeth... Houndvari - Mount: You can be ridden by creatures smaller than Yourself. Houndvari - Gallop: You may spend 2 AP to move 2x+1 Hexes in a straight line. Houndvari - Mule: You can Stack Backpacks of the same type.
Reckless: Your first Attack each turn costs half AP.

item.title: Corge
item.description:
Majestic, cow-sized canines with four paws and two arms... This one has short, stubby legs, and perked up triangular ears Houndvari - Mount: You can be ridden by creatures smaller than Yourself. Houndvari - Gallop: You may spend 2 AP to move 2x+1 Hexes in a straight line. Houndvari - Mule: You can Stack Backpacks of the same type.
Cavalry's Here: Allies within 1 Hex of You gain +Dice on melee Attacks.

item.title: Forestfolk
item.description: Hooved, horned, and/or clawed humanoids who emerged after wild animals consumed Aether spilled during the First War. They are adept nature dwellers and had a part in the emergence of the Houndvari, living up to their Aelf status.... Memorable Meals: You gain insight into the lives and memories of a consumed creature, clarity proportional to the body mass consumed. Quick Adaptation: The first time You take Physical or Magical DMG each combat, gain +1 Resistance to that type of DMG for the rest of that Combat.

item.title: Fireborn
item.description:
Flames bound into humanoid form, created by the Starborn for labor and metallurgy. After the First War, they revolted with the help of Forestfolk and escaped to form their own kingdoms... Light and heat source. Special Diet: You consume Fuel instead of Rations. Fire DMG restores Vitals.
Diminishing Flame: For every point of Vitals missing from Max, base Action Points Regen is reduced by 1.

item.title: Speed
item.description: The maximum amount of Hexes a Character can move by paying 1 AP. Also determines Group Travel Speed on the World map and exploration.

item.title: Aether Sickness
item.description: Aether represents perfect reality and the balance of nature. Over-absorption overwhelms the soul. Characters can only benefit from Aether-Magic healing up to half their Max HP per Sanctuary Rest. Beyond the Cap: Roll a d12 whenever you are healed by Aether. First instance beyond the cap: Sickness only on a roll of 1. Each subsequent instance: Increase the failure range by your Max HP. (e.g., a character with 5 Max HP fails on a 1-6 on their second healing instance beyond the cap). Effects: When subject to Aether Sickness, you enter a catatonic state, inversing the Heroic Bleedout state - Losing 2x AP per HP over 0. (A character with 3 HP, when sick, would lose 6 AP). The Sickness passes after you’ve gone into negative AP, or HP, as you violently rid your system of the excess Aether

item.title: Resolution
item.description: When you wish to undertake an action with a degree of probability or tension (picking a lock, overhearing a conversation), you roll a single d12 as the base, then apply any +Dice and/or -Dice modifiers, and consult the table below:

item.title: Sanctuary Rest
item.description: Places safe from both environmental (weather, terrain) and creature-based threats. It should ideally have some form of enrichment or activity (a library, a forge, etc.). Resting here restores full HP and Armor Pips and grants milestone SP (extra SP from enriched locations).Sanctuary Checklist: Friendly? (No Hostiles aware of you) Comfortable? (Bedrolls, thick moss, pillows) Secured? (Easily Defended, preferably guarded) Insulated? (Safe from the weather and climate) Sanctified? (Against Intrusions) Provisioned? (Food, drink) Unsafe Spots: Resting in an unsafe location (ones that don't meet 4/6 of the above requirements) carries risk (ambush, robbery, etc.). It only restores half of your max HP and Armor Pips and does not grant SP. If you set up a guard duty, those on watch do not gain the benefits of the rest at all.

item.title: Weapons
item.description: Unarmed: 4 AP per swing, 1 damage. Deals self-damage against armored opponents, 0 hex reach. Short: 3 AP for 2 damage, 0 hex reach. You leave the weapon in the target, or pull it out for 1 AP. Medium: 4 AP for 2 damage, 1 hex range. Heavy: 4 AP for 3 damage, with -Dice due to handling, 1 hex range. Bows and other weapons where you hold both the instrument and the missile. These have dedicated Skill Trees. Shortbow Range of 8 Hexes (0-4/4-8/8-12) Deals 1 Damage 3 AP draw cost 1 AP loose cost Longbow Range of 12 Hexes (0-6/6-12/12-18) Deals 2 damage 5 AP draw cost 1 AP loose cost Crossbows and the emerging firearms. These get modifications and attachments instead of skill trees. Crossbow Range of 6 hexes (0-3/3-6/6-9) Deals 1 damage 4 AP draw cost 1 AP fie cost Can be accessorised, at the cost of a Skill Tree: Magical Barrel - mounted at the end of your instrument, it changes your damage type to the Barrels' kind. Pavise - -//-, but ranged attacks against you get -Dice due to cover. Can be left where deployed to bypass movement penalty, and forgo the benefits. Magical Barrel - mounted at the end of your instrument, it changes your damage type to the Barrels' kind. Loading Tool - decrease draw cost by 1. Repeater Crossbow Range of 4 hexes (0-2/2-4/4-6) Deals 1 damage 4 AP draw cost, per bolt 1 AP fire cost, per bolt Can be accessorised, at the cost of a Skill Tree: Pavise - Costs 1 AP to deploy and 2 to stow. Removes long range penalty, movement costs +1 AP if you wish to move with it, but ranged attacks against you get -Dice due to cover. Can be left where deployed to bypass movement penalty, and forgo the benefits. Magical Barrel - mounted at the end of your instrument, it changes your damage type to the Barrels' kind. Extended Barrel – increase your weapon’s range by 2 hexes. Loading Tool - decrease draw cost by 1. Flintlock Range of 5 Hexes (0-3/3-5/5-8) Deals 2 damage 6 AP to reload 1 AP to fire One handed Can be accessorised, at the cost of a Skill Tree: Extended Barrel – increase your weapon’s range by 2 hexes. Magical Barrel - mounted at the end of your instrument, it changes your damage type to the Barrels' kind. Each Space takes 2 points of damage Firing is highly ineffective over larger ranges. 6 AP to reload 3 AP to fire Can be accessorised, at the cost of a Skill Tree: Pavise - -//-, but ranged attacks against you get -Dice due to cover. item.description: Ammunition (Bullet) 1x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot / 1x Copper Ingot + 1x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot / 1x Copper Ingot => 5x Firearm Bullet Ammunition (Bolt) 1x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot + 1x Plank => 3x Crossbow Bolt Mechanical Weapon - Crossbow 2x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot + 2x Plank + 1x Fabric => Crossbow 4x Iron Ingot / 2x Steel Ingot + 3x Plank + 1x Fabric => Siege Crossbow 3x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot + 4x Plank + 4x Fabric => Repeater Crossbow Mechanical Weapon - Firearm 1x Plank + 1x Steel Ingot => Pistol 3x Plank + 2x Steel Ingot / 3x Iron Ingot => Rifle 2x Plank + 4x Steel Ingot / 6x Iron Ingot => Shotty Melee Weapon Xx Iron Ingot / X/2x Steel Ingot / Xx Gold Ingot / Xx Copper Ingot / 2Xx Scrap Metal 4Xx Wood Bundle / X Plank / X Fabric 1x Leather / 2x Bones / 2x Wood Bundle / 1x Scrap Metal / 1x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot / 1x Gold Ingot / 1x Copper Ingot 1st contribute 1:1, unlimited input. 2nd contribute 2:1, still with unlimited input. 3rd contribute 1:1, but are limited input. =<5 Spaces = Short Weapon 6-9 Spaces = Medium Weapon 10+ Spaces = Heavy WeaponEx.: 3x Iron Ingots + 12x Wood Bundles + 1x Gold Ingot = 3 + 3 (6/2) + 1 = 7 Spaces = Medium Melee Weapon. OR 1x Steel Ingot + 1x Fabric + 2x Bones = 2 (1x2) + 1 + 2 = 5 Spaces = Short Melee Weapon. OR 12x Scrap Metal + 4 Plank + 1x Leather = 6 (12/2) + 4 + 1= 11 Spaces = Heavy Melee Weapon Armour Piece Xx Iron Ingot / X/2x Steel Ingot / Copper Ingot / 2Xx Wood Bundle / 2Xx Leather / 2Xx Bones / 2Xx Scrap Metal Xx Raw Mineral (Crystal) / X/2x Gold Ingot / Xx Copper Ingot Y Fabric 1st contribute Physical Armour 1:1, unlimited input 2nd contribute Magical Armour 1:1, unlimited input For every 3 materials spent, 1 Fabric is required (rounding down). Armour (item) Size is determined by dividing the sum of its final materials (including Fabric) by 3.Ex.: 4x Iron Ingots + 12 Raw Mineral (Crystal) + 5 Fabric = 21. 21/3 = 7. The Armour has 4 Physical Pips, 12 Magical Pips, and takes up 7 inventory Spaces. OR 6x Steel Ingot + 4 Gold Ingot + 3 Fabric = 13. 13/3 = 4. The Armour has 12 Physical Pips, 8 Magical Pips, and takes up 4 inventory Spaces. Healing Item 2Xx Various Herbs / 2Xx Various Mushrooms / 2Xx Various Fruit / 4Xx Raw Meat 2Xx Various Herbs / 2Xx Various Mushrooms / 2Xx Various Fruit / 4Xx Raw Meat +2Xx Various Herbs / 2Xx Various Mushrooms / 2Xx Various Fruit / 4Xx Raw Meat Container (Empty) Various Herbs make the effect last 1 turn for every 2 Various Herbs used. Converts perfectly consumable Ore into liquid form for alternative storage solutions. 1x Water 1x Raw Ore (Iron) / 1x Raw Ore (Copper) / 1x Raw Ore (Gold) 1x Raw Ore (Iron) / 1x Raw Ore (Copper) / 1x Raw Ore (Gold) 1x Raw Ore (Iron) / 1x Raw Ore (Copper) / 1x Raw Ore (Gold) = 1x Chunky Ore Blend for every unique Ore used (Requires Container). Crystal Crackers Ration item for the Yig. Sacrifices abundance of Crystal to prepare easy to stockpile Jerky alternative. (1x1) 2x Raw Mineral (Crystal) = 1x Crystal Crackers Speaking of, Crafting skill finalised. It starts with one node then splits into two, and then one of the two splits into two again.CONTAINERS ARE 1D4+1 SPACES LARGELevel 1 - Crafting. You can make use of the basic crafting Kit/Station and learn all recepies associated with it. Level 2A - Alchemy. You learn to make food items and The Healing Item. Also allows use of the Alchemy Kit/Station and recepies associated with it Level 3A - Advanced Alchemy. You learn to make advanced consumables such as specific potions (that grant resistances), and Runes (more on that another time but basically item passives limited at one per) Level 4A - SP SINK 5. Gain +1 Magical Armour Pip. Level 2B - Smelting. You learn to use the Smelting Kit/Station and make ingots from ores you find. Level 3B1 - Armoursmithing, you learn to use the Armour Smithy kit/station and the recepies associated with it Level 4B1 - Armoursmithing. You gain +1 Physical Pip. SP SINK 5. Level 3B2 - Weaponsmithing. You learn to use the anvil/weapon Smithy kit/station and make Drawn weapons (Longbow and Shortbow) as well as Arrows and Arrow Quivers, and melee weapons Level 4B2 - You learn to make mechanical weapons, their ammo and quivers/pouches to hold it I also think that attachments should occupy inventory space while unattached, AND half that amount of space when attached - but this also make the mechanical Weapon more clunky. I think it's a fair price to pay as there's otherwise no limit on attachments per weapon.Now, going a little deeper into the Runes subject. The unorganised thoughts I have in my head regarding them: - Craftable with 2 Crystal + 1 Copper Ingot / 1 Gold ingot + ANY T4 component/relic/artefact/drop (whatever they'll end up being called). Makes them relatively cheap but still scarce. Not sure whether the T4 should dictate the effects of if that should be the crafter's choice. First is more Monster Hunter-y, while second definitely can save the players some grinding - A set and specified list of 10-20 passives that can be applied to any weapon or armour. I think by default every weapon should have 1 Rune slot, BUT: 1. I don't think Mechanical weapons should get one on account of the attachments - this means putting a rune on a mechanical Weapon is significantly costlier than on any other one. 2. I think another specialised Craftable consumable that Alchemy (or maybe armoursmithing so it gets something extra to do?) could make would be a Rune Frame, which just gives +1 Rune slot. 3. To avoid 20 runes per piece of equipment, I think rune slots should have a set size/shape (like a 4x1 line, or 2x2 box), and you can only add a rune slot if it would actually fully overlap with your weapon (and not encroach on any already applied runes) +1 fire resistance / +1 Fire damage - as above with Ice, psychic, Thunder, and every other element except Aether. - +2 Blind Eyes (for the piece of equipment it's applied to, or in general?) great for You and ignoring the crystal growths - +1 AP Regen / -1 AP cost to swing/fire, maybe limited to the first attack every turn. - +1 Physical or Magical Pip / Bypass 1 Physical or Magical Pip when attacking
